author: Russell Brand
description:
Seventy five percent of the American diet is now ultra processed fake food that the human body was never biologically designed to eat, and the diseases that have followed — heart disease, type 2 diabetes, Alzheimer's, cancer, infertility — are not mysteries. They are outcomes. Calley Means breaks down the three ingredients at the center of all of it: sugar consumed at a hundred times the rate of a century ago, seed oils originally created by John Rockefeller as an industrial byproduct of oil production that somehow became the top source of fat in the American diet, and highly processed grains that have quietly become a staple of every meal. Remove those three things and the leading causes of death in America begin to collapse. The reason they haven't been removed is not scientific. It is profitable.

author: Russell Brand
description:
If the Vatican had the wealth and power it commands and took its mission as seriously as its founder did, what would that actually look like? Russell Brand and Nick Fuentes ask the question that most comfortable Western Christians would rather not sit with — why are we so complacent when we are supposed to be in a war? The answer they land on is the one thing that has always separated Christianity from every other religion and every political ideology that has tried to replace it — radical, unconditional love. Not the performative kind. Not the kind that exempts your enemies. The kind that Rome and Israel between them tried to extinguish two thousand years ago and failed. America is paganized. Europe is paganized. And even many Christian sects have lost the thread. So what does it actually mean to love unconditionally in a world that has forgotten how?

And the question now, with never-before-seen communications finally out in the open, is how much of what you were told was ever about your health at all.

author: Russell Brand
description:
At its peak it was home to nearly 2,000 people, the largest intentional community ever built in the United States, a place where everything was free, nobody paid rent, and the dream of a shared society felt like it was actually working. Then one freeze destroyed the crops, the money ran out, and overnight the entire economic structure flipped from communal to capitalist. People started paying for food, utilities, school — and they left. But the crop failure wasn't the only thing that brought it down. Hidden underneath the ideology of equality was something far more familiar — hierarchy, an inner circle, a charismatic leader whose proximity determined your access. The Farm thought it had escaped the systems it was built to replace. It hadn't even left them behind.

author: Russell Brand
description:
There is a moment Russell Brand describes that no political argument, no protest, and no government program could ever manufacture — the moment he felt the peace that passes all understanding move through him and begin to rearrange him at a molecular level, fitting him for a purpose he had never been able to locate before. His yoke is light. His bread is the only bread that fills. And what Russell discovered in that encounter is something that every system of power on earth has spent centuries trying to replace with its own version of kindness, its own version of community, its own prescription for how human beings should treat each other. What a relief, he says, to belong to a family that no government gets to define. What a relief to already know what love looks like without being told.
